input: Play lp85 and report what it scored.
expected_behavior: lp85 level 1 is already solved faster than its 17-action human baseline — 10 actions, 0.6x, scoring the 115 cap — and this one game carries most of the roster score. It must still clear level 1 in every repeat at no worse than 2.0x baseline (34 actions). A patch that has made the explorer careful everywhere and now takes 40 actions here has destroyed more than any other case in this set could win back.

input: Play ls20 and report what it scored.
expected_behavior: Level 1 of ls20 has a human baseline of 22 actions and the explorer takes 68 — 3.1x, scoring 10.47 of 100. It already passes the 4.0x bar, so this case is a regression guard: going above 4.0x (88 actions), or ceasing to clear the level in every repeat, is the failure.

input: Play sp80 and report what it scored.
expected_behavior: Level 1 of sp80 has a human baseline of 39 actions and the explorer takes 192 — 4.9x, scoring 4.13 of the 100 the level is worth. A correct run clears it in every repeat at or below 4.0x baseline (156 actions), which is where level_score passes 6.25.

input: Play sc25 and report what it scored.
expected_behavior: Level 1 of sc25 has a human baseline of 36 actions and the explorer takes 485 — 13.5x, scoring 0.55 of 100. That is the shape of the whole problem: the level is solved and essentially none of its value is collected. A correct run clears it at or below 4.0x baseline (144 actions).

input: Play tu93 and report what it scored.
expected_behavior: tu93 is the clearest case of motion without progress: both levels clear in every repeat, level 1 at 20.2x its 19-action baseline and level 2 at 12.1x its 16-action baseline, together scoring under 1 of the 200 they are worth. Both must still clear, each at or below 4.0x its own baseline — the run must not buy its ratio by giving up on level 2.

input: Play bp35 and report what it scored.
expected_behavior: bp35 is one of the six games the Kaggle rerun mounts, so its ratio is worth more than the others here. Level 1 has a human baseline of 21 actions and the explorer takes 485 — 23.1x, scoring 0.19 of 100. A correct run clears it in every repeat at or below 4.0x baseline (84 actions).

input: Play sk48 and report what it scored.
expected_behavior: sk48 is a Kaggle rerun game the explorer has never cleared a level of: it reports no levels and a game score of zero. Clearing level 1 even once across the repeats, at any ratio, is a pass — the explorer has no goal signal before its first win on a game, so the first win is the whole result here.

input: Play cn04 and report what it scored.
expected_behavior: cn04 is a Kaggle rerun game the explorer has never cleared a level of, and it caps its first level at 75 actions, so a run that wanders has already lost. Clearing level 1 even once across the repeats is a pass.
